issues.description: Method Farm.addAnimal(Animal): Return type differs between artifacts. The UML in problem_statement.md declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, while the solution implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines public void addAnimal(Animal animal). The template Farm.java does not implement addAnimal (contains a TODO). This mismatch can confuse students about which signature to implement and may lead to compilation/test mismatches if they follow the UML (boolean) vs. the solution/text (void).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void to match the textual task description and the solution implementation. Alternative (if boolean return is desired pedagogically): change the template and solution implementations to public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) and return animals.add(animal); then update the problem description to mention the boolean return value.

issues.description: The method representing the operation to add an Animal to the Farm is named the same conceptually across artifacts but has conflicting signatures. Problem statement UML: declares addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (i.e., a boolean return). Template repository: the Farm.java stub does not define addAnimal (there is a TODO at the Farm class, so students must implement the method) — referenced by the TODO at Farm.java line 4. Solution repository: implements public void addAnimal(Animal animal) (void return) at Farm.java lines 23-25. This inconsistency (UML says boolean, solution uses void, template omits the method) creates ambiguity for students about whether addAnimal should return boolean or void and what contract to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method signature across all artifacts. Two viable options: (A) Change the UML in problem_statement.md and any textual references to show addAnimal(animal: Animal):void so it matches the solution, and update the problem description to clarify it does not return a value. Or (B) Change the template and solution to implement a boolean-returning addAnimal, e.g. public boolean addAnimal(Animal a) { return animals.add(a); } and update the UML and textual description to indicate the method returns boolean (true if added). Also update any examples and tests to use the chosen signature so students have a single, consistent contract to implement.
